meta.title: Swedish Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 830 expressions · 200 everyday, 300 particle verbs, 250 idioms, 80 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 830 Swedish set phrases, particle verbs, idioms and proverbs, in four subdecks: 200 everyday phrases, 300 particle verbs, 250 idioms and 80 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Swedish → English (see the Swedish, recall the meaning) and English → Swedish (see an English meaning, recall the Swedish) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Swedish A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Swedish speaker uses as one piece (eller hur, jag vet inte, på väg …). The PARTICLE VERBS are a verb and a particle or a preposition that together mean something the verb alone does not (vara på, skulle vilja, säga till …) — Swedish is built on them, the particle carries the stress, and the card shows the present, past and supine of the whole. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (vet du, stiga upp, på gång …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (som man bäddar får man ligga, en bild säger mer än tusen ord, inget nytt under solen …). Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Swedish sentences contain them, a particle verb being counted with its verb in any form; 485 of the 830 are found there, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. The particle verbs and idioms are the commonest of the many Wiktionary lists, chosen by that same order. Real example sentences come with 479 of the 830 expressions, three apiece for 239, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, forms and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
